staging_before.summary: Common mistakes in reading assessment results, including types, scores, interests, career advice, and professional-help boundaries.
staging_before.content_md:
## Misunderstandings Can Cause More Problems Than Results

An assessment result is usually an interpretive framework. The larger risk often comes from treating the result as identity, ability, destiny, or professional judgment. The purpose of this page is to help users read results more accurately, not to make them believe a label more strongly.

## Misconception One: A Type Is an Identity

MBTI or similar type results can help users observe preference styles, but a type is not an identity. A person cannot be fully defined by four letters or by one type. A type description should be read as a possible set of preference clues, not as a personality ID card.

If some descriptions do not fit, users can treat them as questions to test rather than force themselves to agree.

## Misconception Two: A High Score Is Good and a Low Score Is Bad

Big Five and other dimensional scores are not moral evaluations. A higher or lower tendency can bring advantages and costs in different contexts. For example, higher conscientiousness may support planning and execution, but it may also come with stronger pressure. Higher openness may support exploration, but may make stable processes harder to tolerate.

Scores need to be understood in context, not as simple rankings.

## Misconception Three: Interest Equals Ability

RIASEC / Holland is more focused on career interests and work-environment preferences. It is not an ability measurement. A user may be interested in a type of activity and still need learning, training, and real experience. A user may also have an ability but not want to do that kind of work over the long term.

Career exploration needs to consider interest, ability, opportunity, and practical constraints together.

## Misconception Four: A Result Is Advice

An assessment result is not an instruction. It can point users toward certain directions, but it cannot decide whether they should change jobs, switch majors, resign, or enter a particular industry. Major decisions require more information, including industry research, skill assessment, economic conditions, real experience, and professional advice.

## Misconception Five: Different Models Can Be Mixed Freely

MBTI, Big Five, and RIASEC focus on different questions. MBTI is more about preference style, Big Five about continuous personality dimensions, and RIASEC about career interest. Mixing them into one conclusion can make the interpretation confusing.

A better approach is to clarify the question first: am I trying to understand personality preference, behavioral tendency, or career interest? Different questions call for different tools.

## Misconception Six: Assessment Can Replace Professional Help

It cannot. Assessment cannot perform medical or mental-health evaluation, cannot intervene in emotional distress, and cannot replace professional counseling. If a user is experiencing ongoing distress, crisis, or a serious difficulty, they should seek qualified professional support.

## 误区比结果本身更容易造成问题

测评结果本身通常只是一个解释框架。真正容易造成误解的，是用户把结果当成身份、能力、命运或专业判断。常见误区页的目标，是帮助用户更准确地阅读结果，而不是让用户更相信某个标签。

## 误区一：类型就是身份

MBTI 或类似类型结果可以帮助用户观察偏好风格，但类型不是身份。一个人不会被四个字母或某个类型完整定义。类型描述应被当作“可能符合的一组偏好线索”，而不是人格身份证。

如果某些描述不符合你，可以把它们当成待验证问题，而不是强迫自己认同。

## 误区二：高分就是好，低分就是差

大五人格和其他维度分数不是道德评价。某个维度高或低，都可能在不同场景中有优势和代价。例如，较高尽责性可能有助于计划和执行，也可能伴随更强压力；较高开放性可能有助于探索，也可能让稳定流程更难忍受。

分数需要放在场景中理解，而不是简单排名。

## 误区三：兴趣等于能力

RIASEC / 霍兰德模型更关注职业兴趣和工作环境偏好，不等于能力测量。你可能对某类活动有兴趣，但仍需要学习、训练和真实经验。你也可能具备某项能力，却并不喜欢长期从事相关任务。

职业探索需要同时看兴趣、能力、机会和现实约束。

## 误区四：结果就是建议

测评结果不是行动命令。它可以提示你关注某些方向，但不能替你决定是否转行、换专业、离职或进入某个行业。重大决定需要更多信息，包括行业研究、技能评估、经济条件、真实体验和专业建议。

## 误区五：不同模型可以随便混用

MBTI、大五和 RIASEC 关注的问题不同。MBTI 更偏偏好风格，大五更偏连续人格维度，RIASEC 更偏职业兴趣。把它们混成同一个结论，会让解释变得混乱。

更合理的方式，是先问清楚问题：我想理解人格偏好、行为倾向，还是职业兴趣？不同问题对应不同工具。

## 误区六：测评可以替代专业帮助

不能。测评不能进行医学或心理健康评估，不能干预情绪问题，也不能替代专业咨询。如果你正在经历持续痛苦、危机状态或重大困扰，应寻求合格专业支持。

相关说明可以查看[测评科学](/zh/science)、[方法边界](/zh/method-boundaries)、[信度与效度](/zh/reliability-validity)。相关测评可查看 [MBTI 测试](/zh/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types)、[大五人格测试](/zh/tests/big-five-personality-test-ocean-model)、[霍兰德职业兴趣测试](/zh/tests/holland-career-interest-test-riasec)。

## 常见问题

### 为什么我不像自己的 MBTI 类型？

类型描述是偏好线索，不是完整身份。你可能只符合其中一部分，也可能因为情境或成长经历表现出不同面向。

### 大五人格低分是不是不好？

不是。大五维度不是价值评价。每个维度在不同环境下都有可能带来优势和限制。

### 职业兴趣高是否代表我有能力？

不代表。兴趣说明你可能愿意投入某类活动，能力还需要学习、训练和经验验证。

### 测评结果可以当建议执行吗？

不建议。结果适合转化成问题和观察方向，重大决定仍需要更多现实信息。

### 为什么不同测试给出的感觉不一样？

因为它们关注的构念不同。MBTI、Big Five 和 RIASEC 不是同一种测评。

### 结果不符合我，是不是测试没意义？

不一定。你可以保留有启发的部分，标记不符合经验的部分，并用真实经历继续验证。

snapshot.title: Common Misconceptions
snapshot.content_md:
## Misconceptions can cause more problems than results themselves

An assessment result is usually only an interpretive framework. Misunderstanding is more likely when users treat it as identity, ability, fate or professional judgment. This page aims to help users read results more accurately, rather than believe more strongly in a label.

## Misconception one: A type is your identity

MBTI and similar type results can help users observe preference styles, but a type is not an identity. Four letters or a type cannot fully define a person. Type descriptions are ‘a set of preference clues that may fit’, rather than a personality identity card.

If descriptions do not fit you, treat them as questions to test, rather than force yourself to accept them.

## Misconception two: High scores are good and low scores are bad

Big Five and other dimensional scores are not moral evaluations. A high or low score on a dimension can have strengths and costs in different contexts. Higher conscientiousness may help planning and execution, but also bring greater stress; higher openness may help exploration, but make stable processes harder to tolerate.

Understand scores in context, rather than simply rank them.

## Misconception three: Interest equals ability

The RIASEC / Holland model focuses more on career interests and work environment preferences; it is not a measure of ability. Interest in an activity still requires learning, training and real experience. You may also possess an ability without enjoying the related tasks over the long term.

Career exploration must consider interests, abilities, opportunities and practical constraints together.

## Misconception four: A result is advice

Results are not instructions to act. They can point toward directions worth considering, but cannot decide whether you change careers or majors, leave a job or enter an industry. Major decisions need more information, including industry research, skill assessment, financial circumstances, real experiences and professional advice.

## Misconception five: Different models can be mixed freely

MBTI, the Big Five and RIASEC address different questions. MBTI focuses more on preference styles, the Big Five on continuous personality dimensions, and RIASEC on career interests. Blending them into the same conclusion makes interpretation confusing.

First clarify your question: do you want to understand personality preferences, behavioral tendencies or career interests? Different questions call for different tools.

## Misconception six: Assessment can replace professional help

It cannot. Assessments cannot provide medical or mental health evaluations, intervene in emotional problems or replace professional consultation. If you are experiencing persistent distress, a crisis or major difficulties, seek qualified professional support.

For related explanations, see [Assessment Science](/en/science), [Method Boundaries](/en/method-boundaries) and [Reliability and Validity](/en/reliability-validity). For assessments, see the [MBTI Test](/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types), [Big Five Personality Test](/en/tests/big-five-personality-test-ocean-model) and [Holland Career Interest Test](/en/tests/holland-career-interest-test-riasec).

## Frequently asked questions

### Why don't I seem like my MBTI type?

Type descriptions are preference clues, rather than a complete identity. Only some may fit, and context or growth experiences may bring out different aspects of you.

### Is a low Big Five score bad?

No. Big Five dimensions are not judgments of worth. Each dimension can bring strengths and limitations in different environments.

### Does strong career interest mean I have the ability?

No. Interest suggests you may be willing to invest in an activity. Ability still needs learning, training and testing through experience.

### Can I act on results as advice?

This is not recommended. Turn results into questions and directions for observation; major decisions still need more real-world information.

### Why do different tests feel different?

They address different constructs. MBTI, the Big Five and RIASEC are different assessments.

### If a result does not fit me, does the test have no value?

Not necessarily. Keep the useful parts, mark what does not fit your experience, and continue testing against real experiences.

before.content_md:
## The data discussed on this page

FermatMind's assessment experience may involve responses, results generated from those responses, service data used to support recovery or unlocking, and aggregate statistics about public-page performance.

These categories have different purposes and risks. This page distinguishes private results, records needed to operate the service, and aggregate observations of visits.

## Responses and results

Responses are the choices made in an assessment. Results are the summaries, dimension explanations, or report content generated from those choices. They can be personal because they reflect self-descriptions of personality, interests, behavior, or career preferences.

Private results should not become material for public pages, search engines, sitemaps, llms feeds, public article links, social links, or statistics pages. A result link containing user-specific identifiers should not be treated as public content.

## Support and recovery data

Recovering a result, investigating an unlock failure, handling a refund, or resolving an account issue may require minimum information to locate a request. Email and masked identifiers should be preferred over asking people to post complete order numbers, payment identifiers, result links, or private links from screenshots publicly.

Where additional identification is needed, use the last few characters, a masked order code, or a designated secure method. The specific support fields and handling times depend on the formal Help pages and support rules. Consult the published Help pages for current support requirements.

## Aggregate statistics differ from personal results

Aggregate statistics may help observe visits to a public page, clicks on an assessment entry point, or problems in a flow. These observations support product improvement; they are not publication of personal assessment results.

Analytics should not record private result, order, payment, or history pages, or user-specific links. If such paths appear in analytics, privacy issues should take priority over further growth analysis.

## Retention, deletion, and account requests

The formal privacy policy and support process determine whether deletion can be requested, its scope, handling time, and whether results remain recoverable. Consult the published privacy policy and support guidance for processing times. This page does not promise immediate deletion or that data is never retained.

Identity verification should use a secure channel. Public comments, social messages, or insecure forms should not be the main way to handle private results and orders.

## Scope of this explanation

This page explains assessment-data boundaries and does not replace the formal privacy policy or terms. Retention, deletion scope, and handling depend on formal policies and confirmed support processes; this page makes no universal promise about periods or scopes it does not specify.

## Frequently asked questions

### Should search engines be able to see my results?

Private results and user-specific links should not enter sitemaps, llms feeds, search submissions, or public internal links.

### Does support need a complete order number?

Public pages should not request complete order numbers. Email and masked identifiers or a designated secure method are more appropriate.

### Should analytics see my results?

Analytics should not record private result or order pages. It should be limited to public pages and aggregate behavior.

### Can I request deletion of assessment data?

You can submit a request. Its scope, identity verification, and timing depend on formal privacy and support procedures. This page makes no universal promise about scopes or periods it does not specify.

### Can a result be recovered after deletion?

That depends on the scope and processing of deletion. This explanation does not establish a universal answer; formal support rules apply.

## Related guidance

[Privacy policy](/en/privacy); [Support center](/en/support)

## What Kind of Data This Page Explains

The FermatMind assessment experience may involve several types of data: user response data, result data generated from responses, service data used to support recovery or unlocking, and aggregate statistics used to observe public page performance.

These data types have different uses and different risks. The purpose of this page is to help users understand which information belongs to private results, which information is needed for product operation, and which information exists only as aggregate page-level observation.

## Response Data and Result Data

Response data means the choices a user makes in assessment items. Result data means the result summary, dimension explanation, or report content generated from those responses. This type of data is personal because it may reflect a user's self-description of personality, interests, behavioral tendencies, or career preferences.

Private results should not be used as public page material. They should not enter search engines, sitemaps, llms files, public article links, social links, or statistics pages. Any result link with a user-specific identifier should not be treated as public content.

## Support and Recovery Data

When a user needs to recover a result, resolve an unlock failure, request a refund, or handle an account issue, the system may need the minimum necessary information to locate the request. A safer approach is to start with email and use masked identifying information where possible, rather than asking the user to submit full order numbers, full payment identifiers, full result links, or screenshots containing private links on a public page.

If additional matching information is needed, the preferred approach should use the last few characters, a masked order code, or another system-defined safe identifier. Specific support fields and response timelines should follow the formal Help pages and support rules. Unconfirmed information should remain Unknown.

## Aggregate Statistics Are Different From Personal Results

Public pages may use aggregate statistics to observe product experience, such as how often a public page is visited, whether a public test entry is clicked, or whether a flow has errors. These statistics are used for product improvement and should not be understood as public personal assessment results.

Aggregate statistics should not record private result pages, order pages, payment pages, history pages, or user-specific links. If these paths appear in analytics tools, the privacy issue should be handled before growth analysis continues.

## Data Retention, Deletion, and Account Handling

Whether users can request deletion, which data can be deleted, how long processing takes, and whether results can still be recovered afterward must be confirmed by formal privacy policies and support workflows. If current public documentation does not provide a specific processing period, it should remain Unknown. The page should not promise immediate deletion or permanent non-retention without reviewed authority.

If a user requests deletion, identity should be verified through a safe channel. Public comments, social-media direct messages, or unsafe forms should not be the primary method for handling private results or order issues.

## The Boundary of This Page

## 这页解释哪类数据

FermatMind 的测评体验可能涉及几类数据：用户作答数据、由作答生成的结果数据、用于支持找回或解锁的服务数据，以及用于观察公开页面表现的聚合统计数据。

这些数据的用途不同，风险也不同。数据说明页的目的，是帮助用户理解哪些内容属于私人结果，哪些属于产品运行所需记录，哪些只是聚合层面的访问观察。

## 作答数据和结果数据

作答数据是用户在题目中的选择。结果数据是系统根据作答生成的结果摘要、维度解释或报告内容。这类数据具有个人性，因为它可能反映用户对人格、兴趣、行为倾向或职业偏好的自我描述。

私人结果不应作为公开页面展示素材，不应进入搜索引擎，不应出现在 sitemap、llms、公开文章内链、社媒链接或统计页面中。任何带有用户特定标识的结果链接，都不应被当成公开内容使用。

## 支持和找回数据

当用户需要找回结果、处理解锁失败、退款或账号问题时，系统可能需要最小必要信息来定位请求。更安全的方式是邮箱优先，并尽量使用脱敏识别信息，而不是要求用户在公开页面提交完整订单号、完整支付号、完整结果链接或截图中的私人链接。

如果需要辅助定位，应优先使用后几位、脱敏订单码或系统指定的安全识别方式。当前具体支持字段和处理时限，需要以正式 Help 页面和客服规则为准；当前支持要求请查阅已发布的帮助页面。

## 聚合统计和个人结果不同

公开页面可能使用聚合统计来观察产品体验，例如某个公开页面被访问多少次、某个公开测试入口是否被点击、某个流程是否异常。这类统计用于产品改进，不应被理解为公开个人测评结果。

聚合统计不应记录私人结果页面、订单页面、支付页面、历史页面或用户特定链接。如果统计工具中出现这类路径，应优先处理隐私问题，而不是继续做增长分析。

## 数据保留、删除与账号处理

用户是否可以申请删除数据、删除哪些数据、处理多久、删除后是否还能找回，需要由正式隐私政策和支持流程确认。具体处理周期请查阅已发布的隐私政策和支持说明；本页不承诺立即删除或永久不保留。

如果用户申请删除数据，应通过安全渠道进行身份确认。公开评论、社媒私信或不安全表单不应作为处理私人结果和订单问题的主要方式。

## 本页的边界

本页用于解释测评数据的基本边界，不替代正式隐私政策与条款。数据保留、删除范围与处理方式，以正式政策和经确认的支持流程为准；本页未列出的期限和范围没有统一承诺。

### 我的测评结果会被搜索引擎看到吗？

不应看到。私人结果和用户特定链接不应进入 sitemap、llms、搜索提交或公开内链。

### 客服需要我提供完整订单号吗？

公开页面不应要求完整订单号。更合适的是邮箱优先，并使用脱敏识别信息或系统指定的安全方式。

### 统计工具会看到我的结果吗？

统计工具不应记录私人结果页面或订单页面。它最多应观察公开页面和聚合行为。

### 我可以删除测评数据吗？

可以提出申请。具体范围、身份确认方式和处理时间需要以正式隐私与支持流程为准；未列明的范围和期限没有统一承诺。

### 删除后还能找回结果吗？

这取决于删除范围和系统处理方式。当前公开说明中暂不提供统一结论，应由正式支持规则确认。

snapshot.title: Data Explanation
snapshot.content_md:
## Which data this page explains

FermatMind assessment experiences may involve several kinds of data: users' answers, results generated from those answers, service data for support with retrieval or unlocking, and aggregate statistics used to observe public page performance.

These data have different uses and risks. This page helps users understand what belongs to private results, what is needed to operate the product, and what is merely aggregate observation of visits.

## Answer data and result data

Answer data consists of users' choices in questions. Result data consists of the summaries, dimensional interpretations or report content generated from those answers. These data are personal because they may reflect users' self-descriptions of personality, interests, behavioral tendencies or career preferences.

Private results should not become public page materials, enter search engines, or appear in sitemaps, llms, internal links in public articles, social media links or statistics pages. Any result link with a user-specific identifier should not be used as public content.

## Support and retrieval data

For result retrieval, unlocking failures, refunds or account problems, the system may need the minimum information necessary to locate a request. A safer approach prioritizes email and masked identifiers, rather than asking users to submit complete order numbers, payment numbers, result links or private links in screenshots on public pages.

When additional information is needed, prefer the last few digits, masked order codes or a secure identification method specified by the system. Official Help pages and support rules govern the specific fields and processing timelines. Consult the published help pages for current support requirements.

## Aggregate statistics differ from individual results

Public pages may use aggregate statistics to observe product experiences, such as how often a public page is visited, whether a public test entry point is clicked, or whether a process is abnormal. These statistics improve the product and should not be understood as public individual assessment results.

Aggregate statistics should not record private result pages, order pages, payment pages, history pages or user-specific links. If such paths appear in analytics tools, address the privacy issue before continuing growth analysis.

## Data retention, deletion and account handling

Whether users can request deletion, which data can be deleted, processing times and whether results remain retrievable must be confirmed by the formal Privacy Policy and support process. Consult published privacy and support explanations for specific timelines. This page does not promise immediate deletion or that no data will ever be retained.

Deletion requests should use secure channels for identity verification. Public comments, social media direct messages and insecure forms should not be the main channels for handling private results or orders.

## Boundaries of this page

This page explains basic assessment data boundaries and does not replace the formal Privacy Policy or Terms. Retention, deletion scope and processing methods are governed by formal policies and confirmed support processes. There is no uniform commitment for timelines or scopes not listed here.

## Frequently asked questions

### Will search engines see my assessment results?

They should not. Private results and user-specific links should not enter sitemaps, llms, search submissions or public internal links.

### Does support need my complete order number?

Public pages should not request complete order numbers. A more appropriate approach prioritizes email and uses masked identifiers or secure methods specified by the system.

### Will analytics tools see my results?

Analytics tools should not record private result or order pages. At most, they should observe public pages and aggregate behavior.

### Can I delete assessment data?

You may submit a request. Formal privacy and support processes govern the specific scope, identity verification and processing time. There is no uniform commitment for unlisted scopes or timelines.

### Can results be retrieved after deletion?

This depends on the scope of deletion and how the system handles it. Current public explanations do not provide a uniform conclusion; formal support rules should confirm it.

## Related explanations

[Privacy Policy](/en/privacy) · [Support Center](/en/support)

before.title: FermatMind Giving Plan
before.summary: A corporate responsibility initiative independently undertaken and recorded by FermatMind, with clear boundaries around products, data, and user donations.
before.content_md:
## A continuing public commitment

We want to turn our long-term interest in young people's development, structured decision support, and public issues into corporate action that can be recorded, viewed, and reviewed over time.

From June 1, 2026, FermatMind's plan is to make a charitable donation each day and publish records on its website and public channels. The currently named recipient organization is the United Nations Foundation. The plan describes an intention; completed donations should be assessed against the individual published records.

This initiative is independently undertaken, carried out, and recorded by FermatMind. These are FermatMind's own public records and do not change any external organization's role, status, or responsibilities or imply its endorsement.

## Why we do this

FermatMind focuses on continuing decision-making capabilities in self-understanding, career exploration, and long-term development, beyond a single assessment result.

The giving plan makes this sense of responsibility visible through corporate action that can be documented and reviewed. It connects the platform's development with public issues while keeping boundaries clear.

It does not change assessment logic, report generation, data-processing rules, or the privacy policy.

## The currently named recipient

The United Nations Foundation supports the United Nations in addressing global challenges and advancing the Sustainable Development Goals. Its public mission aligns with FermatMind's interest in long-term responsibility and public issues.

FermatMind independently decides, carries out, and records its donations. Website records describe FermatMind's own actions.

## Published records

The [Daily Giving Ledger](/en/foundation/daily-giving) is available on the website. Use its published entries and monthly archive navigation to check dates, recipients, donation status, public proof status, and public-channel links where disclosed.

Public proof should use only materials approved for public disclosure and should not expose private payment or personal information. The availability of a ledger does not establish that every planned donation has taken place.

## Archive access

Visit the [Daily Giving Ledger](/en/foundation/daily-giving) to browse published records and the monthly archive. The ledger is the place to check the records themselves; this page explains the initiative and its boundaries.

## Public-channel updates

After donations are completed, FermatMind plans to share public records through public channels and link back to the website record pages.

The website records remain the reference for those updates. Screenshots, links, and proof explanations do not change the boundaries of the initiative: these are FermatMind's own public disclosures.

## Important boundaries

The giving plan is FermatMind's independently undertaken corporate responsibility initiative. It does not create a new legal entity, change FermatMind's commercial identity, or change the recipient organization's role or responsibilities.

This page does not collect money from users. Using FermatMind products is not presented as a personal donation by the user or as directly triggering a donation.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the FermatMind Giving Plan?

It is a corporate responsibility initiative independently undertaken, carried out, and recorded by FermatMind. The plan begins June 1, 2026 and aims to make a donation each day, with records published on the website and public channels. Individual records establish what has been disclosed as completed.

### Does this create a new legal entity?

No. It records FermatMind's own corporate actions and does not change its commercial identity.

### What role does the recipient organization have here?

The recipient's name identifies the organization named in the records. FermatMind is responsible for deciding, carrying out, recording, and explaining its own donations. Naming a recipient does not imply endorsement.

### Is each donation restricted to a specific program?

Unless a record expressly discloses designation information, this page does not claim that funds are restricted to a particular project, region, team, or program.

### Does completing a test directly trigger a donation?

The initiative is carried out by FermatMind. This page does not collect money from users or describe product use as directly triggering a donation.

### How can I see the records?

Visit the [Daily Giving Ledger](/en/foundation/daily-giving) and its monthly archive navigation. Public proof should be approved for disclosure and should not expose private payment or personal information.

- [Brand and Usage Guidelines](/en/brand)
- [Assessment Methods and Usage Boundaries](/en/method-boundaries)
- [Policy Overview](/en/policies)
- [Privacy Policy](/en/privacy)
- [Terms of Service](/en/terms)
- [Contact Us](/en/help/contact)
- [Assessments](/en/tests)

### External references

- [United Nations Foundation donation page](https://unfoundation.org/donate/)
- [United Nations Foundation mission and history](https://unfoundation.org/who-we-are/our-mission/)

FermatMind is not only about a single assessment result. Our work is focused on helping young people build clearer self-understanding, career exploration, and long-term decision capacity.

The public-benefit giving plan is one way to turn that long-term responsibility into a visible record. We want this action to remain transparent, reviewable, and bounded. FermatMind decides, records, and explains this giving activity itself. Public records on this page should be read as FermatMind's own company record.

## Latest Records Placeholder

To protect payment security and personal privacy, any public proof materials will redact payment accounts, full transaction numbers, email addresses, phone numbers, addresses, and other sensitive information.

The full daily giving record system will be launched in a later version.

## Full Archive Entrypoint

The full archive entrypoint will be available after the Daily Giving Ledger is launched. A later version is planned to include a daily record index and monthly archive pages for published giving records.

Before the archive system is available, this page only provides the program explanation, boundary note, and future record entrypoint notice.

## Public Updates

After each daily gift is completed, FermatMind plans to publish a corresponding public update and link back to the website record.

## Important Boundary Note

The phrase "public-benefit giving plan" refers to FermatMind's own public record of company giving.

This plan does not create a separate legal body, change FermatMind's business identity, or change the responsibilities of the recipient organization.

FermatMind does not collect money from users for this page. Product use should not be described as a personal donation action.

source_snapshot.content_md:
## 持续的公开行动

我们希望把对青年成长、结构化决策支持和公共议题的长期关注，转化为可以持续记录、可以公开查看、可以长期复盘的企业行动。

自 2026 年 6 月 1 日起，费马测试计划每日完成一笔公益捐赠，并在官网与公共渠道公开记录。当前受赠组织为 United Nations Foundation。计划说明的是行动目标，实际完成情况应以逐条公开记录为准。

本页面记录的是费马测试自行发起、执行和记录的公益捐赠计划。相关记录应理解为费马测试自己的公开记录，不改变任何外部组织的角色、状态或责任，也不代表获得受赠组织背书。

## 为什么这样做

费马测试关注的不只是一次测评结果，而是青年人在自我认知、职业探索和长期成长中的持续决策能力。

公益捐赠计划是我们把这种长期责任外化为公开行动的一种方式。我们希望通过稳定、可记录、可复盘的企业行动，把平台发展与公共议题保持连接，同时保持清晰边界。

这项计划不会改变费马测试的测评逻辑、报告生成方式、用户数据处理规则或隐私政策。

## 当前受赠组织

当前受赠组织为 United Nations Foundation。

United Nations Foundation 关注全球公共议题和可持续发展目标。费马测试选择该受赠组织，是因为其公开使命与我们对青年成长、长期责任和公共议题的关注方向相近。

费马测试自行决定、执行并记录这项行动。官网记录应理解为费马测试自己的企业行动记录。

## 已公开记录

自 2026 年 6 月 1 日起，费马测试计划在完成每日公益捐赠后，逐步公开对应记录。记录内容将尽量包含日期、受赠组织、捐赠状态、公开凭证状态和公共渠道同步链接。

公开凭证应仅使用已获准公开的材料，不应暴露私密支付信息或个人信息。记录系统可访问，不代表每笔计划捐赠均已完成。

[日常公益记录](/zh/foundation/daily-giving)已可访问，可查看已公开记录并通过月度归档导航浏览。

## 完整归档入口

通过[日常公益记录](/zh/foundation/daily-giving)及其月度归档导航，可集中查看已公开的捐赠记录。

本页面说明计划和边界；具体公开记录以记录页为准。

## 公共渠道同步

每日公益捐赠完成后，费马测试计划在公共渠道同步发布公开记录，并回链到官网记录页。

公共渠道内容仍以官网记录为准。任何截图、链接或凭证说明都不会改变本页面的边界：公益相关记录属于费马测试自己的公开说明系统。

## 重要边界说明

本页面中的“公益捐赠计划”指费马测试自行发起、执行和记录的企业社会责任行动。

这项计划不会设立新的法律主体，不改变费马测试的商业主体身份，也不改变受赠组织的角色或责任。

本页面不面向用户收取款项。用户使用费马测试产品的行为，不应被描述为个人捐赠行为。

## FAQ

### Q1：什么是费马测试公益捐赠计划？

这是费马测试自行发起、执行和记录的企业社会责任行动。自 2026 年 6 月 1 日起，我们计划每日完成一笔公益捐赠，并在官网与公共渠道公开记录。

### Q2：这是否意味着费马测试设立了新的法律主体？

不是。本页面记录的是费马测试自己的企业行动，不会设立新的法律主体，也不改变费马测试的商业主体身份。

### Q3：受赠组织在这里扮演什么角色？

受赠组织名称用于帮助公众理解记录指向。费马测试负责自行决定、执行、记录并解释自己的公益捐赠行动。

### Q4：捐赠是否限定给某一个指定专项？

除非未来记录中明确展示具体捐赠指定信息，否则本页面不会声称捐赠资金被限定用于某一个特定项目、地区、团队或专项计划。

### Q5：用户完成测试是否会直接触发一笔捐赠？

不会这样表述。公益捐赠计划由费马测试自行执行。本页面不面向用户收取款项，也不会把用户行为描述为直接触发一笔公益捐赠。

### Q6：如何查看记录？

费马测试计划在官网和公共渠道公开记录。[日常公益记录](/zh/foundation/daily-giving)已可访问，可查看已公开记录并通过月度归档导航浏览。公开凭证应仅使用已获准公开的材料，不应暴露私密支付信息或个人信息。

snapshot.summary: FermatMind's charitable giving plan is a corporate social responsibility initiative independently initiated, carried out and recorded by FermatMind. It does not change FermatMind's product, assessment, data processing or commercial entity boundaries. This page does not collect money from users or describe product use as personal donations.
snapshot.content_md:
## An ongoing public initiative

We hope to turn our long-term attention to young people's development, structured decision support and public issues into corporate action that can be continuously recorded, publicly viewed and reviewed over time.

Starting on 2026-6-1, FermatMind plans to make a charitable donation each day and publish records on its website and public channels. The current recipient is the United Nations Foundation. The plan states an intended action; actual completion is governed by the individual public records.

This page records a charitable giving plan independently initiated, carried out and recorded by FermatMind. The records are FermatMind's own public records: they do not change any external organization's role, status or responsibilities, and do not represent endorsement by the recipient.

## Why we do this

FermatMind cares about more than a single result: we care about young people's continuing ability to make decisions in self-understanding, career exploration and long-term development.

The giving plan is one way to express this long-term responsibility through public action. We hope to connect platform development with public issues through steady corporate action that can be recorded and reviewed, while maintaining clear boundaries.

This plan does not change FermatMind's assessment logic, report generation, user data processing rules or Privacy Policy.

## Current recipient

The current recipient is the United Nations Foundation.

The United Nations Foundation focuses on global public issues and sustainable development goals. FermatMind selected it because its public mission is close to our interests in young people's development, long-term responsibility and public issues.

FermatMind independently decides, carries out and records this action. Website records should be understood as records of FermatMind's own corporate action.

## Publicly released records

Starting on 2026-6-1, FermatMind plans to gradually publish corresponding records after completing each day's donation. Where possible, records will include the date, recipient, donation status, status of public supporting documents and links to records shared on public channels.

Public supporting documents should use only material approved for public release, without exposing private payment or personal information. An accessible record system does not mean every planned donation has been completed.

[Daily Giving Records](/en/foundation/daily-giving) are accessible. You can view published records and browse through the monthly archive navigation.

## Full archive entry point

Use [Daily Giving Records](/en/foundation/daily-giving) and its monthly archive navigation to view published donation records in one place.

This page explains the plan and its boundaries; consult the records page for specific public records.

## Sharing on public channels

After each day's charitable donation is completed, FermatMind plans to share the public record through public channels and link back to the website record page.

Website records remain authoritative for public channel content. Screenshots, links or supporting document explanations do not change this page's boundaries: charitable giving records belong to FermatMind's own public explanation system.

## Important boundaries

The ‘charitable giving plan’ on this page refers to a corporate social responsibility initiative independently initiated, carried out and recorded by FermatMind.

The plan does not establish a new legal entity, change FermatMind's commercial entity identity or change the recipient's role or responsibilities.

This page does not collect money from users. Use of FermatMind's products should not be described as a personal donation.

## FAQ

### Q1: What is the FermatMind charitable giving plan?

It is a corporate social responsibility initiative independently initiated, carried out and recorded by FermatMind. Starting on 2026-6-1, we plan to make a charitable donation each day and publish records on the website and public channels.

### Q2: Does this mean FermatMind has established a new legal entity?

No. This page records FermatMind's own corporate action. It does not establish a new legal entity or change FermatMind's commercial entity identity.

### Q3: What role does the recipient play here?

The recipient's name helps the public understand what the records refer to. FermatMind independently decides, carries out, records and explains its own charitable giving actions.

### Q4: Are donations restricted to a specific designated initiative?

Unless future records explicitly show specific donation designations, this page does not claim that funds are restricted to a particular project, region, team or special initiative.

### Q5: Does completing a test directly trigger a donation?

We do not describe it that way. FermatMind carries out the giving plan independently. This page does not collect money from users or describe user actions as directly triggering a charitable donation.

### Q6: How can I view the records?

FermatMind plans to publish records on its website and public channels. [Daily Giving Records](/en/foundation/daily-giving) are accessible; view published records and browse using monthly archive navigation. Public supporting documents should use only material approved for public release, without exposing private payment or personal information.

before.summary: Start with Order Lookup and email settings. If support is still needed, use an official secure channel and mask private information.
before.content_md:
## Use these official options before contacting support

For report recovery, order lookup, delivery status, and resending a delivery email, start with [Order Lookup](/en/orders/lookup).

For email settings, use [Manage Email Preferences](/en/email/preferences). If you only want to stop receiving emails, use [Unsubscribe](/en/email/unsubscribe) directly.

The personal unsubscribe link in an email also remains valid. Contact a support person if these options do not resolve the issue.

## Information to provide if you still need support

- The purchase email, provided only through an official secure support channel

- If order identification is needed, start with a masked code or last few digits; do not post full order details or private result links publicly

before.title: Frequently Asked Questions
before.summary: Common answers for reports, payment, and account-related requests.
before.content_md:
## Before you contact support

Use the formal recovery and email-control paths before you contact support.

- Go to Order lookup with your order number and purchase email first.

- Use Order lookup for report recovery, order lookup, delivery status, and resend delivery email.

- Use Manage email preferences for email settings. This is separate from report recovery.

- Use Unsubscribe from emails to stop messages, or use the dedicated unsubscribe link inside any email you already received.

- Check your purchase email inbox and spam folder for report links.

- From the order detail page, you can review delivery status, resend the delivery email, and return to Order lookup for purchase-email recovery.

- If payment failed, retry from the order page instead of creating duplicate orders.

- Contact support after these formal paths if the issue is still unresolved.

## Typical support topics

- Report not received after successful payment

- Payment declined or interrupted

- Refund request and eligibility review

- Retake guidance and result sharing

- Business or research usage requests

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I get my report after payment?

Open Order lookup with your order number and purchase email. If the report is ready, the order detail page will show delivery status, report access, PDF download, resend delivery email, and a path back to Order lookup for purchase-email recovery.

### How do email preferences and unsubscribe links work?

Report recovery and email settings are separate. Use Manage email preferences to update email settings. Use Unsubscribe from emails or the dedicated unsubscribe link inside any email to stop messages. If you need a new report email instead, go to Order lookup with your order number and purchase email.

### What should I do if payment fails?

Return to the order page and retry payment from the built-in flow. Avoid creating duplicate orders unless the original order is canceled.

### Can I request a refund?

You can ask support to review your order. Digital-report access and delivery, refunds, duplicate charges, subscription cancellation and abnormal orders follow the [Terms of Use](/en/terms), the Other Policies referred to there, and the purchase-page rules. Submit your order number, purchase email and reason through the official support channel; explain any failed delivery or duplicate charge. Eligibility depends on the applicable order rules and circumstances. This FAQ does not promise a universal refund period, amount or automatic approval.

### Can I use FermatMind tests in my company or research project?

Yes, but usage scope and rights differ by scenario. Please review the dedicated business/research page and contact us for authorization details.

## 联系客服前建议先做

- 退订邮件可直接使用退订页面，也可以继续使用邮件中的专属退订链接

- 先检查购买邮箱收件箱和垃圾箱中的报告邮件

- 进入订单详情页查看交付状态、最近发送情况，并按需重发交付邮件

- 如需购买邮箱恢复，可从订单详情页返回订单查询继续操作

## 高频咨询主题

- 支付成功但未收到报告

- 支付被拒绝或中断

- 退款申请与适用条件

- 是否可重测、如何分享结果

- 企业或研究场景是否可使用

## 常见问题

### 支付完成后如何获取报告？

请先用订单号和购买邮箱进入订单查询。若报告已生成，订单详情页会显示交付状态，并提供查看报告、下载 PDF、重发交付邮件，以及返回订单查询执行购买邮箱恢复的入口。

### 邮件偏好和退订链接如何使用？

### 可以把费马测试用于公司或研究吗？

可以，但不同场景的授权和使用边界不同。请先阅读企业/研究页面，再联系支持获取适配方案。

before.title: Using FermatMind for Business and Research
before.summary: Scope, authorization, and compliance notes for organizational usage.
before.content_md:
## Usage scope

FermatMind supports voluntary self-reflection, team communication and internal learning with a clear purpose, informed participation and a defined visibility boundary. Participants must be able to decline or stop without adverse consequences.

Do not use assessment results for recruitment screening, hiring, promotion, pay, job-fit ranking or exclusion. Team discussion can explore preferences and agreed ways of communicating; it must not assign duties or opportunities from a type or score. Keep individual results private unless the participant gives specific permission.

## Business and research projects

Contact official support with the purpose, participant volume, timeline, needed outputs and data-access plan. Organizational access, research use, billing and delivery require the applicable agreement and privacy safeguards. A public assessment does not itself authorize bulk collection, identifiable research use or a personnel decision.

before.title: Item Design Notes
before.content_md:
## Turning a concept into a question

The central challenge in item design is turning an abstract concept into a question people can answer. Career interests, conscientiousness, and information preferences are not directly visible. Items ask users to describe their responses to particular tasks, situations, or preferences.

The process starts by defining the construct and then designing a set of items to cover different aspects of it. Items collect self-descriptions of understandable situations; they do not read minds.

## Why one item is insufficient

A single item can be affected by misunderstanding, mood, and recent experiences. Someone may answer differently because of a recent event even when that response does not reflect their longer-term tendencies. Assessments should therefore avoid drawing conclusions from one item.

A set of items can observe the same dimension in different situations, allowing the overall pattern to be considered. This does not eliminate all error, but provides a more careful basis than one response alone.

## Similar and reverse-worded items

Questions may seem similar because they examine the same dimension in different settings. For example, liking to plan ahead and finding disorganized processes draining may both relate to order and planning, while one concerns an active preference and the other a response to a situation.

Some assessments use items worded in opposite directions to address mechanical or one-direction response patterns. Whether reverse-worded items are used, how they are scored, and how consistency is checked depend on the particular item bank. Current public documentation does not provide the complete structure of FermatMind's item banks.

## Response options matter

An item includes both its wording and its response options. A forced choice, a five-point scale, an agreement scale, or a situational choice changes how people can express themselves. Too few options may compress differences; too many may increase hesitation.

Do not search for a correct answer. Respond according to your usual experience rather than an ideal self or what others expect.

## Recognizing response bias

Assessments cannot eliminate response bias. People may present themselves favorably, aim for a particular result, be influenced by their current mood, or interpret wording differently. Item design can seek to reduce these problems but cannot guarantee their absence.

Interpret results as patterns under the current items and responses rather than a final judgment about a person.

## Check public documentation and validation evidence separately

Check the public documentation for the specific tool’s version, item count, scoring, and norm status rather than treating all of these as unknown. Disclosure is not evidence that reliability, validity, or a proposed use has been validated; item development, samples, and validation claims require evidence for the relevant version and use.

Related reading: [Assessment Science](/en/science), [Assessment Methods and Usage Boundaries](/en/method-boundaries), and [Reliability and Validity](/en/reliability-validity).

## Frequently asked questions

### Why do some questions look similar?

They may observe the same tendency in different settings. Similarity does not necessarily mean duplication, but the item design must justify their inclusion.

### Should I answer as I am or as I want to be?

Use your usual experience. Answering as an ideal self can produce a picture of your goals rather than your currently observable tendencies.

### Are reverse-worded items intended to catch lying?

They should not simply be understood as a lie detector. They may help examine response consistency or mechanical answering; their specific use depends on the item bank.

### Do more questions always mean better accuracy?

No. Item count, quality, model design, and response fatigue all matter. More items do not automatically make an assessment better.

### Does FermatMind publish item-bank validation figures?

This page does not compile all item-bank validation figures. Specific claims need checkable evidence for the tool, version, sample, and use; item counts or item sources alone do not establish accuracy.

staging_before.title: Item Design Notes
staging_before.summary: How assessment items translate constructs into answerable questions, and why multiple items, similar items, and boundaries matter.
staging_before.content_md:
## How an Idea Becomes a Question

The central challenge in item design is turning an abstract idea into a question that a user can answer. Concepts such as career interest, conscientiousness, or information preference are not things a user can directly see. Assessment needs concrete items that let users observe their responses in certain tasks, situations, or preferences.

This process can be understood as first defining the construct to be observed, then designing a group of items that cover different sides of that construct. Items are not meant to read minds. They collect a user's self-description in situations that are understandable enough to answer.

## Why a Single Item Is Not Enough

A single item is easily affected by interpretation bias, mood, and temporary experience. A user may answer one item differently because of something that happened recently, even if that answer does not reflect a longer-term tendency. For that reason, an assessment should usually not rely on one item for interpretation.

A more stable approach is to design a group of items around the same dimension. Different items observe a similar tendency from different situations, and the final interpretation looks at the overall pattern. This still cannot remove all error, but it is more careful than single-item judgment.

## Why Similar and Reverse-Scored Items May Appear

Users sometimes feel that certain items are asking similar things. This may happen because the items are observing the same dimension from different situations. For example, "I like to plan ahead" and "disorganized processes drain me" may both relate to order and planning, but the first is closer to an active preference and the second to a situational response.

Some assessments may also use items written in the opposite direction to reduce mechanical answering or one-way response patterns. Whether reverse-scored items are used, how they are scored, and how consistency is checked should depend on the specific item-bank design. Current public documentation does not provide the complete FermatMind item-bank structure.

## How Response Options Shape Results

An item includes not only text but also response options. Whether the options are forced choice, a five-point scale, an agreement scale, or a situational choice affects how users express themselves. Too few options may compress differences. Too many options may increase hesitation.

When answering, users do not need to search for the "correct" answer. A better approach is to answer according to their usual state, rather than the ideal self or the image others may expect.

## Response Bias Must Be Acknowledged

Assessment cannot fully remove response bias. Users may present themselves more positively, aim for a certain result, be affected by mood, or interpret item language differently. Item design can try to reduce these issues, but it cannot guarantee that they disappear.

Result interpretation should therefore preserve boundaries: it reflects the pattern under the current items and current responses, not a final judgment about the person.

If item-bank version, item count, item development process, sample information, or validation data are not publicly available, the page should not claim that item design has been validated in a specific way. Where current public documentation does not provide these numbers, they should remain Unknown.

source_snapshot.title: 题目设计说明
source_snapshot.content_md:
## 题目如何从“概念”变成“问题”

题目设计的核心难点，是把抽象概念转成用户能回答的问题。比如“职业兴趣”“尽责性”“信息偏好”都不是用户可以直接看见的东西。测评需要通过具体题项，让用户观察自己在某些任务、情境或偏好中的反应。

这个过程可以理解为：先确定想观察的构念，再设计一组题项来覆盖它的不同侧面。题项不是为了读心，而是为了收集用户对可理解情境的自我描述。

## 为什么不能只靠单个题目

单个题目容易受到理解偏差、情绪状态和临时经验影响。一个用户可能因为最近某件事，对某道题做出与长期倾向不同的回答。因此，测评通常不应依靠单题解释。

更稳妥的方式，是围绕同一维度设计一组题项。不同题项从不同场景观察同类倾向，最后再看整体模式。这样仍然不能消除全部误差，但比单题判断更稳妥。

## 相似题和反向题有什么用

用户有时会觉得某些题在问类似内容。这可能是因为它们都在观察同一维度，但场景不同。比如“我喜欢提前规划”和“混乱流程会让我消耗”都可能与秩序和计划有关，但前者偏主动偏好，后者偏情境反应。

有些测评也会使用方向相反的题项，用来降低机械作答或单一路径回答的影响。是否使用反向题、如何计分、如何检查一致性，需要以具体题库设计为准。当前公开说明中暂不提供 FermatMind 各题库的完整 item bank 结构。

## 量表选项如何影响结果

题目不仅包括文字，也包括选项。选项是二选一、五点量表、同意度量表，还是情境选择，都会影响用户如何表达自己。过少的选项可能压缩差异，过多的选项可能增加犹豫。

用户作答时，不需要寻找“正确答案”。更合适的方式，是按自己通常的状态回答，而不是按理想中的自己或别人期待的样子回答。

## 作答偏差需要被承认

测评不能完全消除作答偏差。用户可能会美化自己、迎合某种结果、受当前心情影响，或因为题目语言理解不同而产生偏差。题目设计可以尽量减少这些问题，但不能保证完全避免。

因此，结果解释时应保留边界：它反映的是当前题目和当前作答下的模式，而不是对一个人的最终判定。

## 分开核对公开说明与验证证据

题库版本、题量、计分与常模状态，应分别查看具体工具的公开说明，不能一概说成未知。公开这些信息不等于已完成信度、效度或用途验证；题项开发、样本和验证结论仍须有对应版本与用途的证据。

相关方法说明可查看[测评科学](/zh/science)和[方法边界](/zh/method-boundaries)。关于信度和效度的解释可查看[信度与效度](/zh/reliability-validity)。

## 常见问题

### 为什么有些题目看起来很像？

它们可能从不同情境观察同一类倾向。相似并不一定是重复，但需要题库设计来证明其必要性。

### 我应该按真实状态还是理想状态回答？

建议按通常状态回答。按理想状态回答可能让结果更像目标形象，而不是当前可观察倾向。

### 反向题是不是在测试我有没有撒谎？

不应简单理解为“抓撒谎”。反向题可能用于观察作答一致性或减少机械作答，但具体使用方式需要题库说明。

### 题目多是不是一定更准？

不一定。题量、题目质量、模型设计和作答疲劳都影响结果。更多题目不自动等于更好。

### FermatMind 是否公开题库验证数据？

本页不汇总全部题库验证数值。具体主张须对应到工具、版本、样本与用途的可核对证据；题量或题目来源本身不能证明结果准确。

snapshot.title: Item Design Notes
snapshot.content_md:
## How concepts become questions

The central difficulty in item design is turning abstract concepts into questions users can answer. ‘Career interests’, ‘conscientiousness’ and ‘information preferences’, for example, are not things users can directly see. Assessments use concrete items to help users observe their reactions to certain tasks, situations or preferences.

The process can be understood as identifying a construct to observe, then designing a set of items covering its different aspects. Items collect users' self-descriptions in understandable situations; they do not read minds.

## Why a single item is not enough

A single item is easily affected by misunderstanding, emotional state and temporary experiences. A recent event may lead someone to answer a question differently from their longer-term tendencies. Assessments should therefore generally avoid interpretation based on a single item.

A more cautious approach designs a set of items around the same dimension. Different items observe similar tendencies in different contexts, before the overall pattern is considered. This still cannot remove all error, but is more cautious than judging from a single item.

## What similar and reverse-worded items do

Some questions may seem to ask similar things because they observe the same dimension in different contexts. For example, ‘I like planning ahead’ and ‘Disorganized processes drain me’ may both relate to order and planning, but the former concerns an active preference and the latter a response to a situation.

Some assessments also use items worded in the opposite direction to reduce mechanical answering or responses that follow a single pattern. Whether reverse-worded items are used, how they are scored and how consistency is checked depend on the specific question bank design. Current public explanations do not provide the complete item bank structures of FermatMind's question banks.

## How response options affect results

Questions include both wording and response options. Two-choice options, five-point scales, agreement scales and situational choices all affect how users express themselves. Too few options may compress differences; too many may increase hesitation.

There is no need to seek a ‘correct answer’. Answer based on your usual state, rather than your ideal self or others' expectations.

## Response bias must be acknowledged

Assessments cannot fully eliminate response bias. Users may present themselves more favorably, seek a particular result, be affected by their current mood or understand the wording differently. Item design can try to reduce these problems, but cannot guarantee their complete prevention.

Interpretations must therefore preserve the boundary: results reflect patterns within the current questions and answers, rather than a final judgment about a person.

## Check public explanations and validation evidence separately

Check each tool's public explanations separately for question bank versions, item counts, scoring and norm status, rather than treating them all as unknown. Publishing this information does not mean reliability, validity or use-specific validation is complete. Item development, samples and validation conclusions still require evidence corresponding to the version and intended use.

For related explanations, see [Assessment Science](/en/science) and [Method Boundaries](/en/method-boundaries). For explanations of reliability and validity, see [Reliability and Validity](/en/reliability-validity).

## Frequently asked questions

### Why do some questions look similar?

They may observe the same kind of tendency in different situations. Similarity is not necessarily duplication, but question bank design must demonstrate why those items are needed.

### Should I answer based on my actual or ideal state?

Answer based on your usual state. Answering as your ideal self may make the result resemble a desired image rather than currently observable tendencies.

### Do reverse-worded items test whether I am lying?

They should not simply be understood as ‘catching lies’. They may observe response consistency or reduce mechanical answering, but the question bank explanation is needed to understand their specific use.

### Are more questions always more accurate?

No. Item count, item quality, model design and response fatigue all affect results. More questions do not automatically mean better results.

### Does FermatMind publish question bank validation data?

This page does not compile validation values for all question banks. Specific claims must correspond to checkable evidence for the tool, version, sample and intended use. Item counts or sources alone cannot demonstrate result accuracy.

before.title: Assessment Method and Boundaries
before.summary: How to use FermatMind assessment results responsibly, what they can support, and where their limits begin.
before.content_md:
## What FermatMind assessments are

FermatMind assessments are structured self-understanding tools. They collect responses, organize them through defined scoring or interpretation models, and turn the result into language that can help people reflect on personality patterns, interests, work preferences, and growth questions.

A result is best read as a working hypothesis about tendencies in a specific context. It is not a permanent identity, a full biography, or a complete measure of a person's ability, character, health, future, or worth.

## What results can support

Assessment results can help with self-observation, communication, career exploration, learning plans, team conversations, and personal review. They can make patterns easier to name, compare, and discuss.

Results are most useful when combined with real-world evidence: past choices, work samples, feedback from trusted people, repeated behavior over time, and the user's current constraints. They should help users ask better questions and plan next steps, not remove judgment from the user.

## What results cannot decide

FermatMind results do not guarantee school admission, employment, promotion, career success, relationship outcomes, income, health outcomes, or any other high-stakes result. They should not be used as the sole basis for hiring, firing, promotion, compensation, admission, financial decisions, medical decisions, legal decisions, or disciplinary action.

Scores, types, labels, and recommended paths can be incomplete or wrong for a particular person. Human development is affected by environment, opportunity, training, health, relationships, incentives, and time. A report cannot capture all of those conditions.

## Medical and high-stakes limits

FermatMind is not a medical diagnosis, psychological diagnosis, therapy service, crisis service, emergency service, or substitute for qualified professional care. Assessment output should not be treated as a diagnosis of depression, anxiety, ADHD, personality disorder, neurodevelopmental condition, or any other health condition.

If a user is in acute distress, has thoughts of self-harm, experiences serious symptoms, or faces a safety risk, they should seek help from local emergency services, licensed clinicians, trusted family members, or other qualified support instead of relying on an online assessment.

## Data and privacy boundaries

Assessment responses, reports, orders, support messages, device logs, and account information may be processed to provide the service, keep it reliable, handle orders, respond to support requests, protect security, and improve product quality. Privacy handling follows the published Privacy Policy and the notices shown in product flows.

Users should avoid entering unnecessary sensitive information into free-text fields. Organizations should not request or expose individual results unless the purpose, authorization, visibility, retention, appeal path, and privacy obligations are clear.

## How to use results responsibly

Use results as structured input for reflection. Start with one or two claims that feel useful, compare them with real behavior, and test a small next step for a defined period. Keep what is useful, challenge what does not fit, and review the result again when circumstances change.

For education, career, clinical, legal, financial, or employment decisions, combine any assessment insight with qualified human judgment, relevant professional standards, direct evidence, and the user's own goals. The assessment is a tool for thinking, not an authority that decides for the user.

source_snapshot.content_md:
## 一、费马测试的测评是什么

费马测试提供的是结构化自我理解工具。用户通过答题、选择或填写信息，系统按照既定的计分、维度或解释模型，把人格倾向、职业兴趣、工作偏好、成长问题等内容整理成更容易阅读和讨论的结果。

测评结果更适合作为一种关于当前倾向的工作假设，而不是固定身份、完整传记或对一个人能力、品格、健康、未来与价值的最终判断。

## 二、测评结果能做什么

测评结果可以用于自我观察、沟通表达、职业探索、学习规划、团队讨论和阶段复盘。它能够帮助用户把原本模糊的感受转化为更清楚的语言，并为下一步行动提供参考。

更可靠的使用方式，是把结果与真实证据结合起来：过往选择、作品表现、身边人的反馈、长期重复出现的行为，以及当前生活和工作条件。测评应该帮助用户提出更好的问题，而不是替用户做决定。

## 三、测评结果不能决定什么

费马测试不承诺升学、就业、晋升、职业成功、关系结果、收入水平、健康结果或其他高风险结果。测评结果不得作为招聘、淘汰、晋升、定薪、录取、金融、医疗、法律、惩戒等重大事项的唯一依据。

分数、类型、标签和推荐路径都可能对某个具体个体不完整或不准确。人的发展会受到环境、机会、训练、健康、关系、激励和时间影响，一份报告无法覆盖这些全部条件。

## 四、医学与高风险场景边界

费马测试不是医学诊断、心理诊断、心理治疗、危机干预、紧急服务，也不能替代合格专业人员的面对面判断。测评结果不应被解读为抑郁、焦虑、注意缺陷、多动障碍、人格障碍、神经发育状况或其他健康状况的诊断结论。

如果用户正在经历明显痛苦、自伤想法、严重症状或安全风险，应尽快联系当地急救资源、医疗机构、持证专业人员、家人或可信赖的支持者，而不是依赖线上测评结果。

## 五、数据与隐私边界

为了提供服务、生成报告、维护稳定性、处理订单、响应支持请求、保障安全和改进产品，费马测试可能处理答题记录、报告、订单、支持沟通、设备日志和账户信息。具体处理方式以已发布的《隐私政策》和产品流程中的提示为准。

用户应避免在自由输入区域提交与测评无关的敏感信息。组织使用场景下，如果需要收集或展示个体结果，应事先明确目的、授权、可见范围、保存期限、申诉路径和隐私责任。

## 六、如何正确使用结果

建议把测评结果当作结构化参考。先选择一两个对自己有启发的判断，与真实行为进行对照，再用一段明确时间测试一个小行动。对有帮助的部分保留，对不符合经验的部分提出质疑，并在环境变化后重新复盘。

涉及升学、就业、医学、法律、金融或组织人事等重要决策时，应把测评洞察与合格的人类判断、专业标准、直接证据和用户自身目标结合使用。测评是思考工具，不是替用户下结论的权威。

snapshot.title: Assessment Methods and Usage Boundaries
snapshot.summary: How FermatMind assessment results can be used, what they cannot replace, and the boundaries of data, privacy and interpretation.
snapshot.content_md:
## One: What FermatMind assessments are

FermatMind provides structured tools for self-understanding. Users answer questions, make choices or provide information, and the system applies established scoring, dimensional or interpretive models to organize personality tendencies, career interests, work preferences and development questions into results that are easier to read and discuss.

Assessment results are best treated as working hypotheses about current tendencies, rather than fixed identities, complete biographies or final judgments about a person's abilities, character, health, future or worth.

## Two: What results can do

Results can support self-observation, communication, career exploration, learning plans, team discussion and periodic review. They can turn vague impressions into clearer language and provide a reference for further action.

A more reliable approach combines results with real evidence: past choices, the quality of work produced, feedback from others, recurring behavior over time, and current living and working conditions. Assessments should help users ask better questions, rather than make decisions for them.

## Three: What results cannot decide

FermatMind does not promise educational admission, employment, promotion, career success, relationship outcomes, income levels, health outcomes or other high-risk outcomes. Results must not be the sole basis for major matters such as hiring, elimination, promotion, salary setting, admission, finance, medicine, law or disciplinary action.

Scores, types, labels and recommended paths may be incomplete or inaccurate for a particular individual. Development is affected by circumstances, opportunities, training, health, relationships, incentives and time; a report cannot cover all of these conditions.

## Four: Boundaries in medical and high-risk settings

FermatMind is not medical or psychological diagnosis, psychotherapy, crisis intervention or an emergency service, and cannot replace an in-person judgment by a qualified professional. Results should not be read as diagnoses of depression, anxiety, attention deficits, hyperactivity disorders, personality disorders, neurodevelopmental conditions or other health conditions.

If you are experiencing significant distress, thoughts of self-harm, severe symptoms or safety risks, contact local emergency resources, a medical institution, a licensed professional, family members or a trusted supporter promptly, rather than relying on an online assessment.

## Five: Data and privacy boundaries

To provide services, generate reports, maintain stability, process orders, respond to support requests, protect security and improve products, FermatMind may process answer records, reports, orders, support communications, device logs and account information. The published Privacy Policy and notices in product flows govern the specific processing practices.

Avoid submitting unrelated sensitive information in free-text fields. In organizational settings, purposes, authorization, visibility, retention periods, appeal channels and privacy responsibilities should be clarified before collecting or displaying individual results.

## Six: How to use results appropriately

Treat results as a structured reference. Choose one or two observations that seem useful, compare them with real behavior, and test a small action over a defined period. Keep what helps, question what does not fit your experience, and review again when circumstances change.

For important decisions involving education, employment, medicine, law, finance or organizational personnel, combine assessment insights with qualified human judgment, professional standards, direct evidence and your own goals. An assessment is a thinking tool, rather than an authority that draws conclusions for you.

before.content_md:
This page brings together FermatMind's main policies, privacy explanations, assessment boundaries, and support links. It helps you find information about data processing, service use, assessment methods, results privacy, the giving plan, and support.

It does not replace individual policies. Refer to the full explanation on the relevant page for specific terms, data-processing rules, and service boundaries.

## Privacy and data processing

Read the [Privacy Policy](/en/privacy).

It explains data processing in product use, assessments, result recovery, support, and basic analytics, including purposes, storage, user rights, cookies, and analytics tools.

FermatMind seeks to reduce unnecessary processing. This overview provides links and a high-level introduction; the privacy policy contains the specific rules.

## Terms of service

Read the [Terms of Service](/en/terms).

They explain the basic rules for using the website, assessments, reports, content pages, and related tools, including paid services, report use, user responsibilities, content boundaries, and service limitations.

Results, reports, and career guidance are materials for structured self-exploration and decision support. They do not promise particular life, career, income, employment, academic, or other outcomes.

## Assessment methods and boundaries

Read [Assessment Methods and Usage Boundaries](/en/method-boundaries).

FermatMind focuses on personality, career interests, cognitive tendencies, and structured decision support. Results may help organize questions, identify tendencies, compare directions, and support discussion.

Use them as references for self-understanding and communication. Do not rely on them alone in situations requiring professional review, formal institutional judgments, or decisions with high-risk consequences.

## Results and report privacy

Read the [Privacy Policy](/en/privacy) and [Assessment Methods and Usage Boundaries](/en/method-boundaries).

Assessment results, result recovery, and related private information should not become publicly indexed pages. Recovery and credential-verification entrypoints are private technical paths rather than parts of a public content directory.

Do not disclose personal result identifiers, order details, recovery information, or other information identifying private records on public pages, social platforms, or third-party sites.

## Cookies, consent, and tracking

Read the cookie, analytics-tool, and user-consent explanations in the [Privacy Policy](/en/privacy) for the applicable information. This overview directs you to those explanations.

## Giving-plan boundaries

Read the [FermatMind Giving Plan](/en/foundation).

The plan is a corporate responsibility initiative independently undertaken, carried out, and recorded by FermatMind. It is part of FermatMind's own public disclosures and does not change its commercial identity, product boundaries, assessment methods, or data-processing rules.

It does not collect money from users or describe product use as a personal donation. Refer to disclosures on the official website for records, and keep giving records separate from assessment, user-data, and privacy boundaries.

## Contact and support

- [Support Center](/en/support)
- [Frequently Asked Questions](/en/help/faq)
- [Contact Us](/en/help/contact)

Use support and contact pages for questions about privacy, terms, assessment limits, result recovery, giving-plan boundaries, or content accuracy. Do not include identity-card numbers, bank-card numbers, full addresses, health information, or unrelated sensitive information in your initial message.

- [FAQ](/en/help/faq)
- [Contact](/en/help/contact)

If you have questions about privacy, terms, assessment boundaries, report lookup, public-benefit giving boundaries, or content accuracy, use the support and contact pages. source_snapshot.content_md:
本页面用于整理费马测试的主要政策、隐私说明、测评边界和支持入口。它是一个导航型页面，帮助用户快速找到与数据处理、服务使用、测评方法、结果隐私、公益捐赠边界和联系支持相关的说明。

本页面不替代各独立政策页面。具体条款、数据处理规则和服务边界，应以对应页面的完整说明为准。

## 隐私与数据处理

请阅读：[隐私政策](/zh/privacy)

隐私政策说明费马测试如何在产品使用、测评流程、结果找回、客服支持和基础分析场景中处理用户数据。它也会说明数据使用目的、保存方式、用户权利以及 Cookie / 分析工具相关说明。

费马测试会尽量减少不必要的数据处理。本页面只提供政策入口与高层说明，具体数据处理规则应以隐私政策正文为准。

## 服务条款

请阅读：[服务条款](/zh/terms)

服务条款说明用户使用费马测试网站、测评功能、报告服务、内容页面和相关工具时的基本规则。它也会说明付费服务、报告使用、用户责任、内容边界和服务限制。

测评结果、报告内容和职业建议应被理解为结构化自我探索与决策支持材料，而不是对人生、职业、收入、录用、学业或其他结果的确定性承诺。

## 测评方法与边界

请阅读：[方法与边界说明](/zh/method-boundaries)

费马测试关注人格、职业兴趣、认知倾向和结构化决策支持。测评结果可以帮助用户整理问题、发现倾向、比较方向和形成讨论素材。

这些内容适合作为自我理解与沟通参考，不应被单独用于需要专业人员审阅、正式机构判断或高风险后果的场景。

## 结果与报告隐私

请阅读：[隐私政策](/zh/privacy) 与 [方法与边界说明](/zh/method-boundaries)

测评结果、报告找回和相关私密信息不应被设计为公开索引页面。结果找回与凭证验证入口属于隔离的私密技术路径，不作为公开内容目录的一部分。

用户不应在公开网页、社交平台或第三方页面主动暴露个人结果编号、订单信息、找回信息或其他可识别私密记录的内容。

## Cookie / Consent / Tracking

请阅读[隐私政策](/zh/privacy)中的 Cookie、分析工具和用户同意机制说明。本总览页为这些说明提供入口。

## 公益捐赠计划边界

请阅读：[公益捐赠计划](/zh/foundation)

费马测试的公益捐赠计划是费马测试自行发起、执行和记录的企业社会责任行动。它属于费马测试自身的公开说明体系，不改变费马测试的商业主体身份、产品边界、测评方法或用户数据处理规则。

该计划不面向用户收取款项，也不会把用户使用产品的行为描述为个人捐赠行为。公益相关记录应以官网页面公开披露内容为准，并应保持与产品测评、用户数据和隐私边界相分离。

## 联系与支持

可访问以下页面：

- [支持中心](/zh/support)
- [常见问题](/zh/help/faq)
- [联系我们](/zh/help/contact)

如果你对隐私、服务条款、测评边界、报告找回、公益捐赠边界或内容准确性有疑问，可以通过支持与联系页面提交问题。请不要在首次联系时提交身份证号、银行卡号、完整住址、健康信息或其他与问题无关的敏感个人信息。

目前费马测试没有在本次 PR 中新增独立的 Cookie / Consent / Tracking 页面。相关说明继续通过隐私政策中的 Cookie、分析工具和用户同意机制部分承接。

如果后续需要独立的 Cookie 或追踪政策页面，应单独准备内容、路径、索引策略和可见说明，不应在本政策总览页中临时生成新的独立路由或结构化数据。

## 公益捐赠计划边界

请阅读：[公益捐赠计划](/zh/foundation)

费马测试的公益捐赠计划是费马测试自行发起、执行和记录的企业社会责任行动。它属于费马测试自身的公开说明体系，不改变费马测试的商业主体身份、产品边界、测评方法或用户数据处理规则。

该计划不面向用户收取款项，也不会把用户使用产品的行为描述为个人捐赠行为。公益相关记录应以官网页面公开披露内容为准，并应保持与产品测评、用户数据和隐私边界相分离。

## 联系与支持

可访问以下页面：

- [支持中心](/zh/support)
- [常见问题](/zh/help/faq)
- [联系我们](/zh/help/contact)

如果你对隐私、服务条款、测评边界、报告找回、公益捐赠边界或内容准确性有疑问，可以通过支持与联系页面提交问题。请不要在首次联系时提交身份证号、银行卡号、完整住址、健康信息或其他与问题无关的敏感个人信息。
